candidates.title: Draft invoice fields for bookkeeper review

demandEvidence.chore: Bookkeepers and small finance teams retype vendor invoice details from email into a spreadsheet.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Hi all, sharing a workflow I built for bookkeepers and small finance teams who still retype vendor invoices from email into a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A beginner can test extraction from sample PDFs into a spreadsheet, but no attached implementation source documents this workflow.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: bookkeeping firms may pay for less invoice re-entry; this post does not establish customer payment or willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can extract a few fields from synthetic invoice PDFs; vendor formats and accounting accuracy need human review.

autonomy.reason: PDF intake and draft field extraction could repeat, but a bookkeeper must verify values and resolve exceptions; no implementation reference is attached.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly describes bookkeepers retyping emailed vendor invoices into spreadsheets and shares a workflow, but gives limited evidence on frequency or outcomes.

candidates.reason: Assessed a narrow PDF-to-draft-fields experiment, but the equal-weight mean is 5.6, below the 6 threshold. No supplied implementation reference supports the mechanics. The second n8n assignment is the same post and chore.

candidates.title: Draft reviewed translations of technical decisions

demandEvidence.chore: Help translate an Architecture Decision Record into additional languages.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I welcome constructive feedback, and welcome help with the translations.

ease.reason: A student can draft one source section into a chosen language with a general language model, but no supplied implementation reference documents translation support.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional teams maintaining multilingual technical decisions might pay for reviewed translation help; this request establishes no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can draft one short section from operator-supplied text; language accuracy and terminology need a qualified human reviewer.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop can draft and flag uncertain phrases, while a bilingual reviewer must check meaning and approve every translation; no reference supports automation.

evidence.reason: The public post explicitly welcomes help with translations, but gives no target languages, source text, volume, or repeated demand details.

candidates.reason: Assessed a narrow proposed service that drafts one ADR section in an operator-selected language for bilingual review. Its equal-weight mean is 4.6, below the 6 threshold; the discussion does not specify language, volume, or a paying customer, and no implementation reference is supplied.

rejected.title: Azure operations with CeruleanToolbox

rejected.title: Use a collected job-seeker contact list
rejected.reason: The post asks what to do with a collection of personal email addresses and names. A service using applicant contact data creates privacy risks, and the source establishes no safe bounded task; the personal data must not be processed.
